I had renewed my oath to save my sister.
But I was not allowed to run straight down that road.

Work was not the reason. My leave from the company had to be extended once more.

The senior head had declared that the hair-raising ceremony would be held.

Under Minato clan law, the succession to <ruby>ritual officiant<rt>ritual officiant</rt></ruby>—that is, <ruby>priestess-princess<rt>priestess-princess</rt></ruby>—takes place when the girl chosen for the next generation reaches a fixed age. Not before that age. Not after.

Hikaru had fallen ill just before the succession rite. For the senior head, this must have been the biggest regret of his old age. His last great task was about to be settled, and the disease came from the side and spoiled it.

But Doctor Mengele's treatment had put Hikaru's body on the road to recovery. Since then, not one fit.

In the hair-raising ceremony, what the successor must do is only this: perform the appointed rites in the appointed way. Complicated, tedious, yes, but no skill is required, no personal judgment. Even Hikaru as she is now could do it, if an attendant stays beside her.

So the senior head was thinking, naturally, this chance we are not letting go. The doctor had barely left for home before the old man had fixed the date.

For my part, I wanted Hikaru to rest first and get her strength back. The ceremony runs half a day, and the burden on the body is not small. That was exactly why it had been impossible until now.

Even now, far from safe. But the doctor's invitation had put us under a very big obligation. After <ruby>receiving<rt>receiving</rt></ruby> such a favor, neither my foster mother nor I could speak strongly to the senior head's face.

With careful support, perhaps we could make Hikaru's burden lighter...
Thinking like this, we compromised, unwillingly, and obeyed what the senior house wanted.

And today—

妹を救うと、心も新たに誓い――
　しかし、ただその為に邁進する事は許されなかった。

　仕事があるから、ではない。
　会社への休暇願いは、延長を余儀なくされた。

　本家が、髪上げの儀の実施を宣言したからだ。

　皆斗家法において、湊斗の<ruby>祀司<rt>しし</rt></ruby>――即ち<ruby>巫姫<rt>かんなぎ</rt></ruby>の継承
は、次代たるべき女子が一定の年齢に達するをもって
行うものとされている。
　その年齢より前でも、後でもならない。

　継承儀礼――髪上げの儀を目前にして光が病に倒れ
たことは、本家が老境に入って迎えた最大の痛恨事で
あったに違いない。当代の、最後の大事が片付こうと
したところで、横槍を差されてしまったのだから。

　だが、メンゲレ博士の治療によって光の肉体は快方
に向かった。
　あれ以来、発作は一度も起こしていない。

　髪上げの儀の際、継承者がすべきは定められた儀礼
を定められた通りにこなすだけだ。それは複雑にして
煩雑だが、別に技術も自己判断も必要ない。
　今の光でも、介添人が付けばできる事だった。

　本家にしてみれば、この機を逃してなるものか――
というところであったのだろう。
　博士が帰国するや否やのうちに、もう儀式の日取り
まで決めてしまっていた。

　俺としては、今しばらくは光を休ませ、体力を取り
戻させてからにしたかった。
　髪上げの儀は半日にも渡り、体力負担は少なくない。
だからこれまでは無理だったのだ。

　今とても、まだまだ危うい。
　だが、博士の招聘で大恩を<ruby>蒙<rt>こうむ</rt></ruby>った以上、俺も養母も
本家に面と向かって強い事は言えなかった。

　心を配って補佐すれば、光の負担も軽くしてやれる
だろう……。
　そう考え、やむなく妥協して、本家の要望に従った。


　そして、今日――――

Whenever I heard my foster mother recite the ritual prayer, it was magnificent. Inside that flat, level tone there was a depth no one can describe.

Such chanting becomes complete only after years, after thousands and tens of thousands of repetitions. The rule is that the congregation keeps their faces lowered while it goes on, but even without the rule, every head would have bowed by itself.

From the last seat, I slid my eyes along the floor and examined the situation. Discourteous, yes, but unavoidable. I had no formal qualification to attend, and since I was sitting here anyway, I could not be careless with my duty.

Beyond the senior head and the important persons of the Minato houses, seated in two columns, was Hikaru, behind her mother.

She leaned back in a chair, vacant, lending her ears to the prayer. ...For the moment, no abnormality. By now fatigue must have piled up from the rites before this main ceremony in the sanctuary, but it had not yet crossed her limit.

That chair followed no ritual etiquette whatsoever, and it had <ruby>greatly<rt>greatly</rt></ruby> offended the senior head. Still, it was necessary. If she could simply have been laid down, that would be a different matter.

At this rate the rite should end safely. But no carelessness.

To avoid irritating the senior head's nerves any further, we had to be ready to act immediately if anything happened. I took my eyes away, but all my attention stayed on Hikaru.

養母の祝詞奏上はいつ聴いても見事なものだった。
　平板な調子の中に得も言われぬ深みがある。

　何年にも渡り、何千回何万回と繰り返して、初めて
完成する詠唱だ。
　奏上中、参列者は面を伏せて待つのが決まりだが、
そんなものが無くとも自然と頭は下がったろう。

　末席から、床の上を滑らせるようにして視線を投げ、
様子を窺う。
　非礼だが仕方ない。本来参列の資格を持たないにも
拘わらず列席している以上、役目に手は抜けなかった。

　本家をはじめ、皆斗諸家の要人らが左右二列に分か
れて居並ぶ向こう。
　母に付き従う格好で、光がいる。

　座椅子に背をもたれさせ、茫としながら祝詞に耳を
預けているようだった。……今のところ、異変はない。
　この祭殿での本儀礼に先立つ諸儀で既に疲労が蓄積
している筈だが、まだ限度を超える程ではないようだ。

　あの座椅子は礼法に沿うものである筈もなく、本家
の不興を買うこと<ruby>夥<rt>おびただ</rt></ruby>しかったが、やはり必要な措置で
はあった。
　寝転がしておいても良いならまた話は変わるが。

　この分ならば、最後まで無事に済むだろう。
　しかし油断はできない。

　本家の神経をこれ以上逆撫でしない為にも、もし何
かあった際には迅速に対処できるよう備えておかねば
ならなかった。
　俺は視線を外しつつも、光の様子に意識を集めた。

My foster mother finished the prayer without a single error. In an ordinary festival, only offerings of sacred food and tamagushi branches would come next.

Today was different. Next came the rite commonly called the Presentation, the heart of the hair-raising ceremony.

The dignitaries of the senior Minato houses withdrew once.◆
...Then they came back.

In warrior costume.
Carrying swords.

They were armed・・. Only with ceremonial equipment, of course.

Then the ceremony went back one step, to the beginning. The sacred doors, the doors before the divine seat, would be opened again.

Naturally those doors were already open. They had been opened before the prayer, because a prayer offered to the enshrined deity is meaningless if the doors are not opened first, no?

But behind the doors that open in an ordinary rite, there stands one more pair: the Inner Sacred Doors.

These open only for very important rites, like this hair-raising ceremony. What is sealed behind them does not meet outside air even once in a year.

Thick iron doors, like the gate of a castle. A few pieces of war gear, nearly antique, seemed to tremble with nerves at the sight, and gave out small metallic sounds.

Everybody at the center of the Minato clan knew it. The meaning of their weapons. The meaning of the iron doors.

As the form requires, my foster mother used the sacred keysacred key to undo the lock. A hard, heavy sound announced the release of something・・.

She put the key back and shuffled forward on her kneesadvanced upon her knees to open the doors. She took the appointed position, laid her hands on them and began.

At the same moment, every attendee, myself included, bent forward and chanted the warning crywarning cry: Ooooooh.

Once for each of the two doors.
The Inner Sacred Doors stood fully open.

And beyond them, the deepest secret of the Minato house was revealed.

養母の祝詞が滞りなく終わる。
　常の祭事であれば、この後は神饌や玉串を奉るだけ
だ。

　だが今日は違う。
　この次には『顔見せ』と通称される、髪上げの儀の
肝と言うべき祭礼が入る。

　皆斗の歴々が一度退場。◆
　……やがて戻る。

　武家装束に身を固め。
　太刀を携え。

　彼らは武装・・していた。
　あくまで儀礼用のものに過ぎないが。

　そして儀式は一度、始まりへと戻る。
　再び、御扉――神前の扉を開くのだ。

　無論、それは既に開かれている。
　祝詞の奏上の前に。祝詞は祭神に捧げるのだから、
その前に扉を開かねば意味がない。

　だがその際に――つまりは通常の祭儀において開か
れる御扉の奥には、もう一枚の、別の御扉があるのだ。
　奥御扉と云う。

　これはこの髪上げの儀など、特に重要な祭事でしか
開かれない。
　扉の中に封じられたものは年に一度も外気と交わら
ないのだ。

　分厚い鉄扉はさながら城門である。
　骨董品も同然の戦支度が幾つか、それを見てか緊張
に震えて細かな金属音を鳴らし立てた。

　皆斗一族の枢要たる彼らは皆、知っている。
　自らの武装の意味も。鉄の奥御扉の意味も。

　作法通り、養母が御鑰みかぎを用いて門の錠を外す。
　重く固い音が、何か・・の開放を告げた。

　養母は鑰を戻し、今度は扉を開けるために膝進しっしん。
　所定の座に着き、手を掛ける。扉を開き始める。

　それに合わせて、列席者（俺を含む）は一斉に前傾。
　おおおおぅ――と警蹕けいひつを合唱する。

　左右の扉を開けるため、それを二回。
　奥御扉の開扉が完了する。

　そうして――その向こう。
　皆斗家の最秘は、顕れていた。

One was a <ruby>silver<rt>silver</rt></ruby> queen ant.
One was a <ruby>crimson<rt>crimson</rt></ruby> spider.

Both had the shape of insects and the size no insect should have. Their bodies were equal to a human being's.

Made of steel. Steel hammered with technique at the very limit.

<ruby>Sword-armor<rt>tsurugi</rt></ruby>.
And not the <ruby>mass-produced suits<rt>kazuuchi</rt></ruby> that rule the battlefield of today.

They can be completed only when a smith gives his whole body and soul.
<ruby>True-forged sword-armor<rt>shinuchi</rt></ruby>.

Since ancient times, and still today, owning a sword-armor is the exclusive privilege of the warrior class. Yet whatever happened to the Minato clan's own station over the years, they had kept these two suits and passed them down, unused. In complete secrecy.

The Minato clan took root in this land after receiving a command from the <ruby>Emperor<rt>emperor</rt></ruby> to seal an <ruby>evil<rt>evil</rt></ruby> thing. These suits of sword-armor were <ruby>that thing<rt>・・</rt></ruby>, the eternal duty of the clan for all generations.

Their <ruby>names<rt>names</rt></ruby> and origins I did not know in detail. I had only heard that they must never be released. But one look and the reason was clear. The atmosphere around them was monstrously unnatural, full of the smell of <ruby>calamity<rt>calamity</rt></ruby>.

Ten thousand words are not equal to this one sight. Anybody would decide that these must stay sealed for all eternity.

Touching them: forbidden.
Speaking of them: forbidden.

The greatest taboo of the Minato clan.

Their shining steel carried no bloodstain, not even dust. Beautiful, and terrible, it made the flesh <ruby>shudder<rt>shudder</rt></ruby>.

も<ruby>怖気<rt>おぞけ</rt></ruby>を震う……。

A casual signal from my foster mother pulled me back from the luster of the metal. She was holding Hikaru up, somehow getting her to stand, and trying to <ruby>guide<rt>guide</rt></ruby> her to the front of the sword-armor.

Only a few steps. But for Hikaru as she is now, cruel enough. If anything was going to happen, this was the most dangerous moment. This was no time for gaping.

I collected myself and put my attention on Hikaru's back. Maybe the practice for this day, loosening her arms and legs, was bearing fruit. Half carried by my foster mother, she moved one unsteady step at a time, but she moved.

Something like walking, a motion the body has learned, she can apparently still manage if another person prompts it. If the priestess-princess had to carry her successor on her back, the presentation would have looked quite poor, so this was very lucky indeed.

Wobbling, barely, with great difficulty, Hikaru reached the front of the divine seat. The breath of relief that filled the sanctuary then probably belonged to everybody except Hikaru herself.

The main business of the day, the Presentation, was nearly done. The two suits of sword-armor that receive the rites had now been <ruby>formally informed<rt>formally informed</rt></ruby> that the priestess-princess of Minato worship was changing to a new one.

Everyone's relief was natural.

—Perhaps that was the <ruby>error<rt>error</rt></ruby>.

A sudden loud noise made everybody present jump—in mind and in face only. Nobody there had so little self-control as to actually jump.

Instead, all eyes gathered on one spot: the feet of one elderly attendee, whose face had gone appalled.

There was a piece of metal lying there. An ornament of his sword, dropped by some accident.

The senior head's gaze, <ruby>soaked<rt>saturated</rt></ruby> in rage, stabbed through him. The old man, in a panic, picked up the ornament and put it inside his clothes.

—That was all. Just that.

But the abnormality of that moment did not stay only so small.

I had witnessed <ruby>it<rt>・・</rt></ruby>. How it came about, I do not know.

Did Hikaru react to the noise and move <ruby>that way<rt>・・・・・</rt></ruby>? Or did my foster mother, who was supporting her, turn round in surprise and make <ruby>it happen<rt>・・・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>?

The process, unknown.
The fact, present.

Hikaru's fingertips had caught on the silver ant, the sword-armor that must never be touched, not even during the rite.

Three persons, three intentions.
We handed them across with our eyes.

The senior head's furious look, like a destruction beam, was without doubt the strongest. My foster mother's was the most practical.

"We saw nothing."

............

In the end, there was nothing else to do. The senior head let out one breath through grinding teeth. I did the same, with a bitter smile.

If the sword-armor had grown huge at the instant of touch and started breathing fire, that would be a different matter. Nothing of the kind had happened. Getting angry would achieve nothing. The immediate job was to finish the ceremony safely.

The senior head probably had no method except to keep telling himself this argument until he believed it. I felt sympathy for the old clan chief, a man who values obeying the rules above everything. He would not welcome my sympathy, of course.

At the least, we owed him a peaceful continuation from here. With that intention, I returned my attention to Hikaru.

—At that instant.
The <ruby>final abnormality<rt>・・・・・</rt></ruby> came.

　偽りを捨てた真なる武！

　光の道は閉ざされておらぬ！

　その道を進んでくれよう。
　世界を滅ぼし神の座に即つこう。

　父を取り戻すために!!
